subject: hedgehogs
one_liner: Quill is an autonomous ground-mobility stack for hedgehogs. Your hedgehog keeps walking. The road becomes our problem.
brand_voice_notes: Straight-faced automotive press release. The company has classified a live animal as a vehicle and never once acknowledges that this is strange. Everything is a trim level, a firmware version, a supervised feature, or a recall. Range is measured in metres, charge is measured in worms, and the road-crossing problem is discussed with the gravity of a fatality report, because it is one. No jokes are ever landed on. Nothing is winking. The nearest thing to an admission is a footnote about supervision requirements.

hero.sub: Quill is an autonomous ground-mobility stack for hedgehogs. Kerb to kerb, unsupervised is coming, supervised is now. Your hedgehog keeps walking. The road becomes our problem.

features.title: Full Self-Crossing (Supervised)
features.blurb: The stack takes over at the kerb and returns control at the far verge, typically in under nine minutes. Supervised means a competent adult must remain at the roadside for the duration of the crossing. We are aware this was the original problem.

features.title: Sentry Mode
features.blurb: When a hedgehog rolls into a ball, Quill classifies it as parked and begins recording four metres in every direction. Footage is retained for thirty days. The vehicle cannot end the session, because to end the session it would have to unroll.

features.title: Over-the-air firmware
features.blurb: Updates ship at 03:00, mid-forage, when the fleet is at its most available. Version 12.4 removed kerb ascent. It is on the roadmap. Deferring an update is permitted three times, after which the hedgehog is updated.

pricing_tiers.name: Long Range
pricing_tiers.tagline: Two roads and a fence the neighbours consider permanent.
perks: Supercharger access, three mealworm depots, all in Surrey

pricing_tiers.name: Plaid
pricing_tiers.tagline: The hedgehog is no longer the slowest thing in the garden.

testimonials.quote: The 03:00 update removed his ability to climb the step onto the patio. Support tells me the step was never a certified surface. He sat at the bottom of it until half four.
testimonials.name: Marguerite Ellery
testimonials.title: Volunteer Hedgehog Rehabilitator, Wirral Branch

testimonials.quote: He balled up on Tuesday and Sentry Mode recorded my neighbour for eleven hours. I have watched all of it. I would not describe the experience as a feature.
testimonials.name: Yusuf Bright
testimonials.title: Chair, Lower Cadley Hedgehog Highway Committee

testimonials.quote: We reserved in March. The chassis arrived in August in two boxes, and one of the boxes was a wheel. She has crossed nothing. The app says she is en route.
testimonials.name: Dr Peter Nkemelu
testimonials.title: Consultant Ecologist, Verges and Central Reservations

demo_screen_concept: The in-vehicle console: a night-mode driving visualisation of a single hedgehog mid-crossing on a residential B-road, rendered top-down in CSS as a wet asphalt lane with kerbs, a drain grate and a painted centre line. The hedgehog is a small ovoid puck travelling the crossing path. Around it, the perception layer draws cyan bounding brackets on detected objects with classification labels and confidence figures: KERB 0.99, DRAIN GRATE 0.97, VAUXHALL CORSA (PARKED) 0.94, BADGER 0.71, UNKNOWN OBJECT 0.38 on a cat. A left instrument rail carries charge (in worms), range in metres, ground speed in metres per hour, and cabin temperature. Interactivity: an ENGAGE toggle that runs Full Self-Crossing and animates the puck kerb to kerb with a live progress readout, a driving-profile segmented control (Chill / Standard / Assertive) that changes the speed and the disengagement copy, Sentry Mode which balls the vehicle, freezes the crossing and flips the console into a recording state, clicking any detected object to open its classification card, and a persistent over-the-air update banner that can be deferred exactly three times before it installs itself.

images.rationale: Full budget spent. Hero earned it outright: the design direction is photographic automotive press-configurator, and a manufacturer page is carried by one enormous night product shot, so the hedgehog is photographed like a press car on wet asphalt. Demo assets skipped because the demo_screen_concept is an in-vehicle driving visualisation, a rendered UI screen built entirely in CSS, and a photograph inside it would fight the perception layer. Remaining three went to the testimonial plates as unit portraits: the owner quotes are human, so the bracket-framed photograph is the vehicle under review rather than the reviewer, captioned with the owner's name in mono. All four passed vision judging on the first attempt.

design_direction.style: Photographic automotive press-configurator, night-shift dark mode. The page is staged as the product site of a heavily funded autonomous-mobility company that has decided the hedgehog is a vehicle and files the road under solved. A flat wet-asphalt slate ground (#12161A) runs the whole page with no gradients, no aurora washes, no glass, no blur panels, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no paper chrome and no print rules: surfaces are flat fills one shade lighter (#181D22) inside 1px hairline borders (#252C32) at a uniform 4px radius, corners kept near-square because this company builds hardware. Structure comes from three things only: full-bleed photography at press-kit scale, hairline-ruled instrument wells, and enormous quiet type. The organizing move is the press plate: each section is a wide photographic or CSS-built plate with a monumental single-clause claim set beneath it and a row of specification figures under a hairline, the way a manufacturer publishes a vehicle rather than the way a startup publishes a landing page. The core motif is the perception bracket: four 1px cyan corner ticks drawn at the corners of a frame, never a full border, wrapping every photograph, testimonial headshot, spec well and pricing tier, each carrying a small wide-tracked mono label and a two-decimal confidence figure, so every element on the page reads as something the vehicle has detected and classified rather than something a designer placed. The second motif is the charge bar: a row of 24 thin vertical cells, filled cells in charge green and unfilled at 14% opacity, used as the range meter, the list bullet, the pricing-tier gauge and the crossing-progress indicator, so every quantity on the page is expressed as a state of charge. One charge green (#3BE08A) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every primary CTA, one word per headline, and the filled charge cells, always as a flat flood with slate knocked out of it. One rationed perception cyan (#35C8E8) is quarantined strictly to the perception layer (bounding brackets, classification labels, confidence figures, the UNKNOWN OBJECT state, live detection dots) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only second colour on the page is always the machine telling you what it thinks it is looking at. Sora sets the wordmark and headlines in wide geometric grotesque at monumental sizes with manufacturer confidence, tracking tightened to -0.03em at display sizes and full stops kept on the claims. Manrope carries plain, faintly owner's-manual body copy at 17px with a 1.6 line-height. Every figure that pretends to be vehicle telemetry (range in metres, ground speed, worm charge, confidence scores, firmware versions, tier prices) is set in Martian Mono with tabular figures inside inset slate wells one shade darker than the surface, so it reads like the instrument cluster, not marketing. Motion is manufacturer-restrained: a single headlamp sweep crosses the hero once on load, perception brackets snap in 3px at their corners on hover with the cyan label fading up, charge cells fill left to right once on scroll, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur, no gradients, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no hairline print frames, no didone engraving, no split-flap numerals, no hatch fills, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no catalog stitching, no mirrored type, no engraved seals, no emoji. Reads like a company that files a live animal under 'chassis' and considers the B-road a legacy interface.
design_direction.archetype: Interactive configurator / EV manufacturer product page staged as an automotive press site: full-bleed night vehicle-photography hero under a monumental geometric claim with a specification strip in mono, three feature plates alternating photographic plate and perception readout, testimonial plates with bracket-framed headshots and owner credentials, three trim tiers laid out as a configurator ladder with charge-bar gauges, closing CTA band, handoff to the in-vehicle crossing console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: One headlamp sweep across the hero on load; perception brackets snap 3px outward at their corners on hover with the cyan classification label fading up; charge cells fill left to right once on scroll with a 24ms per-cell stagger; CTAs depress 1px on press with the green flood darkening; the live detection dot pulses on a 4s cycle; sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger. Everything gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed 16:9 night photograph of a single hedgehog on wet asphalt, lit like a press car: one hard key light raking across the quills, cold reflected road sheen underneath, deep slate falloff behind. A slate-to-transparent scrim runs the bottom third so the monumental Sora claim sits in the lower-left with the charge-bar range meter and a mono spec strip beneath it. Perception brackets sit at the photograph's corners with a MODEL H / CONFIDENCE 0.98 label. No text is rendered in the photograph itself.
